paragraphs: The core of advertising sales work is not the vague notion of 'being good at chatting', but turning a client's promotional objectives, audience and budget into executable media placements, dayparts or digital advertising plans, and keeping records of quotes, schedules, contracts and commitments. Judging fit should rely on observable task behaviour and working conditions, not personality labels; the exercises and checklists on this page were designed by the editors from public occupational sources for self-exploration, and do not constitute criteria for hiring, screening or ability assessment.

A stronger signal is: you are willing to keep prospecting for clients, you can ask questions before recommending media, you can explain audience, price, specifications and expected results clearly, and you can maintain CRM and follow-up cadence under rejection, quotas and deadlines. A single mock-client exercise with a debrief record can test this: whether constraints were clarified, whether the plan is deliverable, whether the quote is accurate, and whether any commitment went beyond your authority.

If you often promise results without evidence, dislike proactively contacting strangers, find it hard to verify contract details, or treat one rejection as personal failure, this kind of work may steadily drain you; different media, client types and commission systems significantly change the experience. Before judging whether you are willing to carry quota pressure and a rejection cadence over the long term, first test your performance and energy cost with one complete mock client-development and proposal exercise.
Assessments and exercises serve only as a reference for self-exploration, and cannot predict hiring, competence or future performance.

paragraphs:
Section title｜The working environment and ways of working of advertising sales agents
Direct answer｜Advertising sales agents sell specific media placements, dayparts or digital inventory to businesses or individuals, and are accountable for closing and for accounts. The work consists mainly of high-frequency external communication, presentations and quoting, requires carrying quotas, client rejection and strict deadlines, is mostly full-time, and may involve travelling to visit existing and prospective clients.
Common organisations and locations｜Advertising sales agents are employed by advertising agencies, media companies and platforms, publishing and broadcasting organisations, and corporate marketing departments; the work mostly alternates between the office and client visits, with travel arranged around clients.
Work materials and systems｜Common materials include client briefs, media kits and rate cards, placement and daypart specifications, schedules, proofs, sales contracts and campaign data; frequently used tools are CRM, office and presentation software, and media or campaign delivery platforms.
How the work is organised｜The work proceeds through 'prospecting—needs interviews—plans and quotes—proposal presentations—contracts and launch—collections and renewals', with progress reviewed against quota and scheduling milestones.
Deadlines and work intensity｜Intensity centres on monthly or quarterly quotas, scheduling launches and contract milestones: O*NET work context shows that for this occupation 79% of workers face strict deadlines every day, 64% make decisions every day, and 81% use telephone conversations every day.
Collaboration and reporting lines｜They usually collaborate with client decision-makers, internal sales supervisors, media operations, creative or production, finance collections, and legal and compliance; special price approvals and release reviews rest with authorised personnel.
Review and chain of responsibility｜Quotes, discounts and commitments are approved and recorded according to organisational authority; creative release, platform review and legal opinions are confirmed by the corresponding authorised parties, and sales cannot substitute for them beyond its authority.
Quality and job requirements｜Quality depends on whether client constraints were clarified, whether the plan and quote are deliverable and consistent in basis, whether commitments are verifiable, whether records are traceable, and on quota attainment and collection status.

'Actual organisational adoption' looks at whether the organisation really puts the tool into its processes. items.title: How do the entry-level positions and early tasks for advertising sales agents compare?

values: Education and preparation

The BLS Occupational Outlook states that entry to this occupation usually requires only a high school diploma or equivalent, with no related work experience required and typically moderate-term on-the-job training; some employers require or prefer a bachelor's degree.

O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three; occupations in that zone generally require vocational training, related experience or an associate degree—this is a general description of the job zone, not a uniform requirement for every newcomer in this occupation. BLS lists no typical related experience for this occupation, and the two bases cannot be interchanged.
Certification and authorisation

The general U.S. occupational material checked for this page lists no single universal licence, which does not prove that all regions or advertising activities need no permit. Product certification cannot replace quoting, discount or release authorisation.
Verifiable preparation items include media knowledge, CRM use and compliance training records, and the organisation's internal scope of quote and commitment approval.
Work context
O*NET work context shows that for this occupation 79% of workers face strict deadlines every day, 64% make decisions every day, and 81% use telephone conversations every day.

73% consider dealing with external customers or the public extremely important, and 84% use email every day, indicating that the work is dominated by high-frequency external communication and quota pressure.
Common systems and tools
Employer job postings mention office, presentation and design tools most often: Microsoft Office about 17%, Excel about 16%, PowerPoint about 13% and Canva about 8%.

Next are Outlook and Adobe Creative Cloud (about 7% each) and Salesforce (about 5%); mention frequency only shows how often they appear, and does not mean they are required for the job or indicate proficiency.

values: Task statement and input material

Fixed case (all fictional): a two-month campaign for a new store of the chain gym 'Chendong', targeting 1,200 unique valid trial-class sign-ups, with a total budget of 300,000 yuan. Audience priority is the office-worker population within 3 km of the store; the statement sets a cap of CPA250 yuan per valid sign-up. Practice only; not a real business or price.

Media kit V1 (all fictional, two months, tax and production included, no other fees): elevator screens listed at 150,000 yuan, authorised at 8 tenths of the listed price = 120,000 yuan; light boxes 125,000 yuan, 8 tenths of the listed price = 100,000 yuan; app splash screens 100,000 yuan, 8 tenths of the listed price = 80,000 yuan; the three-package schedule runs weeks 1—8, with inventory available but subject to confirmation before signing. Simulated results: screens 400, light boxes 320 and splash screens 200 sign-up records, with no check for cross-channel duplication, validity or source attribution; actual spend equals the three-package quote, with no refunds or additional charges.

Deliver two plans, five needs questions, a price/discount/schedule verification table, contract and performance-statement boundaries, and a one-page debrief; the two plans are all three packages at 300,000 yuan, and elevator screen plus splash screen at 200,000 yuan, with no sign-up volume promised for either plan.
Task requirements

Using the same case, write out the client's objectives and constraints, the matching media mix and rationale, the quote and schedule, and the cost estimate, and mark which claims must go back to the client or the media to be confirmed.
Provide a one-page note: which judgements have public evidence, which are your assumptions, and what you would check first if first-period results fall below target.
Reference approach

Reference judgement: the audience radius of 3 km is a stated assumption; exposure, visibility and deduplication information is missing, so it cannot be concluded that elevator screens have a lower exposure cost or that splash screens have a better causal effect. First ask about the valid sign-up rule, deduplication method, channel attribution, creative approval and confirmation of price and inventory; public occupational material supports only the task background.

Quote check: 150,000×0.8=120,000, 125,000×0.8=100,000, 100,000×0.8=80,000, total 300,000; alternative plan 120,000+80,000=200,000. The three-package V1 price is authorised only by the task statement, and price or schedule changes require separate approval. The total of 920 sign-up records is not equal to unique valid sign-ups, and cannot be treated as a target commitment.

The exercise was designed by this page's editors, and the client, media prices, budget and results are all fictional; the O*NET links below support only the task background, not the statement or the figures.
